sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess a wording detail (body, temple or altar) from Christ's quoted line. No earlier card gives the baker anything to reason from, so the right pick comes down to luck.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The card quotes 'the first' and 'the second' without saying what they are. Verse 9's first sentence ('Here I am, I have come to do Your will') is left out. The baker has no way to tell what is being taken away and what is being established, so the moment doesn't make sense.
sonnet.rule: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

sonnet.problem: The question says 'The old sacrifices came year after year. But...', which rules out the wrong answer 'yearly'. The contrast also signals that 'once' is right.
sonnet.rule: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
